In 1859, America and Britain almost went to war. Over one pig.
On San Juan Island, both countries claimed the land, and their settlers lived side by side.
One day, American farmer Lyman Cutlar found a pig eating his potatoes. So he shot it.
The pig belonged to a British company. Cutlar offered ten dollars. The British wanted a hundred.
They threatened to arrest him. So the Americans sent in soldiers.
Soon, over four hundred American troops and fourteen cannons faced five British warships, with more than two thousand men.
The British governor wanted to land troops and fight.
But the admiral refused, saying he would not start a war between two great nations, over a pig.
Both armies stayed on the island for twelve years, without firing a shot.
In 1872, the German Kaiser settled it. The island went to America. And the only casualty was the pig.
